source.reason: The FE/VUMAT framework is the study-wide model for this alloy under MAF; it uses the MAF-0 (0-pass solutionized) state as the initial condition (σ_0 = 380 MPa, d_0 = 50 μm, ρ_0 = 0.79 × 10^15 m^-2) and Table 4 material parameters.

simulation_method.value: 3-D finite element simulation of multiaxial forging (MAF) using the modified Johnson-Cook constitutive model (Eq. 6) implemented via a VUMAT user subroutine; explicit dynamic technique

potential_model_or_database.value: Modified Johnson-Cook constitutive model incorporating dislocation density and grain size effects (Eqs. 6–8); model parameters from Table 4

boundary_and_initial_conditions.value: 3-D model dimensions 30 mm × 20 mm × 20 mm; die and punch treated as discrete rigid bodies, workpiece as a deformable body; mesh size 0.6 mm (mesh-sensitivity analysis); 41,382 C3D8R hexahedral elements (8-node) with reduced integration and hourglass control; punch controlled displacement of 10 mm in the Y (height) direction while the die is fixed; workpiece free to move in X (flow) direction, constrained in Z by the die wall; friction coefficient 0.15 between workpiece and rigid bodies; steady-state MAF simulated by mapping deformation fields from previous passes.

validation_against_experiment.value: Simulated dislocation density, grain size and yield strength compared with experimental values at MAF-1, MAF-3 and MAF-5 (and initial MAF-0 state); model agrees well up to ~3 passes but underestimates yield strength at 5 passes; simulated yield strength depends on depth from the surface (maximum at centre).

source.reason: Eq. 4 gives the Hall-Petch grain-boundary strengthening contribution; k is reported as 2374 MPa·μm^0.5 for a 50–13 μm range.

model_note.value: Grain-size-strengthening constant k calculated as 2374 MPa·μm^0.5 (for a grain-size range 50–13 μm).

source.reason: Eq. 5 gives the Taylor dislocation strengthening; the constants α, M, G and b are reported.

model_note.value: α = 0.24, M = 3.0, G = 61 GPa; Burgers vector b = 0.259 nm for the FCC austenite.

source.reason: Eq. 7 describes dislocation density evolution with strain; k1 and k2 obtained by curve fitting and ρ_0 taken as the MAF-0 dislocation density.

model_note.value: Empirical relation (Eq. 7) fitted to dislocation density vs equivalent strain; for this study k1 = 7.9 × 10^15 m^-2 and k2 = 1.813.

unmapped_findings: MAF-0 (solutionized and water-quenched, 0 MAF pass) is the reference/baseline state against which the strengthening contributions of the forged states are measured; all dislocation- and grain-refinement strengthening increments are quoted relative to MAF-0 (0 Pass shows '-' for both contributions).

For the MAF-0 (0 pass) condition, all strengthening parameters are already included in σ_0 (380 MPa); grain-boundary and dislocation strengthening only become explicit contributions in subsequent MAF passes.
The alloy possesses very high ductility (greater than 70% at room temperature and greater than 95% at 300 °C) as well as high formability, motivating its use in the MAF study.
MAF-0 is the initial annealed/solutionized state with the (111) peak most intense in XRD (before texturing changes to (220)); the sample is strongly textured before MAF.
The material could only be forged a total of five times before breaking on the sixth attempt; MAF-0 corresponds to the initial annealed state before any forging pass (equivalent strain 0).
